items.rationale: Each deep tree is nearly unbiased but noisy; averaging cancels the random part of the error, so variance falls and bias stays about the same. Picking b or c shows M2, that averaging makes the trees more accurate on average rather than less noisy.
rho*sigma^2 = 0.25*9 = 2.25 and (1-0.25)*9/3 = 2.25, so the variance is 4.5. An answer of 3 is sigma^2/B, which wrongly assumes independent trees (M3).
Random feature subsets stop every tree from splitting on the same strong features, so trees are less alike (lower correlation rho), which lowers the floor rho*sigma^2.

items.rationale: Every leaf predicts a mean of training targets, so the average of trees stays inside the training target range and is flat beyond the last split. Saying it continues the upward trend shows M1.

With rho = 0.4 the variance is near its floor rho*sigma^2 well before 500 trees; the (1-rho)*sigma^2/B term is already tiny. Choosing a or d shows M3 (variance falls like 1/B); choosing b shows M5 (more trees overfit more).
